metrics_descriptions.Cost: Breakdown of residency status (In-State, Out-of-State, WUE), tuition tier, and expected financial aid impact.
metrics_descriptions.Support: Availability and quality of academic advising, tutoring centers, freshman retention networks, and student success resources.
metrics_descriptions.Social: Weekend party environment, Greek life prevalence, off-campus house/bar scenes, and overall nightlife density.
metrics_descriptions.Weather: Count of pleasant/comfortable outdoor days during the core academic school year (Sept–May), excluding extreme heat, snow, or heavy rain.
metrics_descriptions.Biology: Institutional research funding (NIH/NSF), lab access, pre-health tracks, and proximity to biotech corridors.
metrics_descriptions.CLS: Alignment of biology curriculum with California Clinical Laboratory Scientist (CLS) prerequisites (e.g., Hematology, Quant Chem) and clinical rotation pipelines.
metrics_descriptions.Spirit: Game day culture, D1 sports tradition, stadium energy, and collective student body pride.
metrics_descriptions.Admissions: Admissions: Selectivity, acceptance rates, test score profiles, and overall competitiveness of the admissions process.
metrics_descriptions.CultureShock: Cultural transition and similarity to Southern California (lifestyle shift, regional dynamics, student body demographic balance).
metrics_descriptions.Outdoors: Proximity to outdoor recreation (beaches, trails, ski resorts, rivers) and access to active student lifestyle amenities.
metrics_descriptions.GoHome: Travel logistics back to San Diego (direct flight availability, drive times, airport proximity, and travel costs).
metrics_descriptions.Safety: Campus security infrastructure, Clery Act crime statistics, surrounding city crime rates, and off-campus environmental safety.

profile.topology: Flat, coastal campus built on a bluff directly adjacent to the Pacific Ocean; exceptionally bike-friendly with extensive dedicated paths and flat terrain. Outdoors: Steps from the Pacific Ocean for immediate surfing, paddleboarding, and beach volleyball; 20 minutes to Santa Ynez Mountains for world-class trail hiking and mountain biking; zero local ski resorts (3+ hours to Mammoth).
profile.airport_distance: 10 miles (~15 min drive) to Santa Barbara Municipal Airport (SBA).
profile.transit_options: MTD local bus network serves campus heavily, though bikes and walking are the primary modes of transport for students.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: Laid-back beach town culture anchored directly by Isla Vista (IV)—a densely packed, legendary student enclave right outside the campus gates where streets are swarming with bikes, local surf shops, and casual food spots.
profile.housing_status: Freshmen are housed in diverse coastal residence halls like Manzanita and San Nicolas with immediate ocean views. Off-campus housing is hyper-concentrated in Isla Vista high-density student apartments and multi-unit houses, where properties rent out nearly a year in advance and students typically share rooms or pack tightly into close quarters.
profile.medical_access: No on-campus teaching hospital, but connected via regional transit and close proximity to Cottage Health medical networks and local biotech research centers.

academics.carnegie_classification: R1 Doctoral University (Very High Research Activity - AAU Member)
academics.biology_and_pre_med: World-class Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology (MCDB) & Ecology/Ecology/Marine Biology (EEMB) labs; exceptional research funding via NIH/NSF.
academics.clinical_and_medical_access: No on-campus teaching hospital, but connected via regional transit and close proximity to Cottage Health medical networks and local biotech research centers.
academics.flagship_programs: Biomolecular Science & Engineering, Marine Biology, Physics, Chemical Engineering.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$43,937 (In-State CA). Final cost is largely fixed unless eligible for need-based aid.
details.Support: High-performing infrastructure featuring a 93% freshman retention rate and an 83% graduation rate, reflecting exceptionally strong student success systems.
details.Social: Legendary Isla Vista street and house party culture right on the ocean.
details.Weather: ~220 nice days. Mild coastal sun, minimal bad days
details.Biology: Top-tier R1 research; world-class molecular, cellular, and marine biology labs with strong West Coast biotech placement.
details.CLS: Pure theoretical bio; lacks clinical electives like Hematology and Quant Chem.
details.Spirit: No football team, but partially salvaged by a surprisingly massive, rowdy D1 men soccer culture that pulls thousands of students to Harder Stadium.
details.Admissions: Hard: ~30% acceptance rate with heavy emphasis on unweighted GPA. Applicants should expect to have above 3.8 unweighted GPA to be competitive.
details.CultureShock: Identical coastal SoCal beach culture (Isla Vista), outdoorsy lifestyle, and easy drive/flight home.
details.Outdoors: Unmatched daily access to coastal surfing, beach cruisers, and an active ocean lifestyle.
details.Safety: Isolated, heavily controlled coastal campus bubble with very low local crime rates.

test_scores.policy: Not considered for admission, even if submitted

profile.topology: Picturesque rolling campus tucked right against the foothills of the Rocky Mountains with gentle slopes, beautiful stone pathways, and iconic outdoor gathering quads. Outdoors: Immediate walking access to the Flatirons for elite trail running and rock climbing; world-class skiing at Eldora (45 mins) and I-70 resorts (Vail/Copper within 1.5–2 hours); Boulder Creek path runs directly through campus.
profile.airport_distance: 28 miles (~40 min drive) to Denver International Airport (DEN) via regional highway and direct airport bus lines.
profile.transit_options: RTD regional bus system and the on-campus HOP transit route connect students seamlessly across Boulder and to local trailheads.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A classic picturesque mountain-town city feel. The campus flows right into 'The Hill' (a dense student commercial strip with pizza joints and cafes) and is a short walk from the upscale, brick-paved Pearl Street Mall. It feels distinctly upscale, active, and outdoors-obsessed.
profile.housing_status: Freshman housing features unique residential academic programs (RAPs) clustered around main campus. Off-campus housing in Boulder is notoriously expensive and fiercely competitive, requiring students to look months ahead for rentals in local complexes or shared suburban-style houses further from the central quad.
profile.medical_access: Campus medical services available via Wardenburg Health Center; proximal to Boulder Community Health facilities.

academics.carnegie_classification: R1 Doctoral University (Very High Research Activity - AAU Member)
academics.biology_and_pre_med: BioFrontiers Institute powerhouse; deep federal funding and direct pipelines into the Boulder-Denver biotech and medical technology hub.
academics.clinical_and_medical_access: Campus medical services available via Wardenburg Health Center; proximal to Boulder Community Health facilities.
academics.flagship_programs: Molecular, Cellular & Developmental Biology, Aerospace Engineering, Biochemistry, Environmental Studies.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$64,452 - $68,440 (Out-of-State). Does not participate in WUE, but offers automatic non-resident merit scholarships based on GPA. Cost could lower slightly.
details.Support: Strong student retention engine with an 89% retention rate and a 74% graduation rate, ensuring reliable institutional support.
details.Social: Lively Pearl Street and The Hill, but less formal Greek dominance than the SEC.
details.Weather: ~155 nice days. Cold snowy winters offset the crisp sunny days
details.Biology: BioFrontiers Institute powerhouse; deep federal funding and direct pipelines into the Boulder-Denver biotech/medical device hub.
details.CLS: Heavy research bio; missing clinical electives; requires external post-grad prereqs.
details.Spirit: Passionate Folsom Field crowd and prime Big 12 atmosphere, but sports dont totally rule campus life.
details.Admissions: Target: Moderate competitiveness (~80% acceptance rate); values AP rigor and personal essays heavily.
details.CultureShock: High sun and huge SoCal outdoor match (hiking/skiing); very smooth transition despite altitude.
details.Outdoors: World-class access for mountain biking, climbing the Flatirons, and weekend ski trips.
details.GoHome: Easy: 5hr trip via 2.5hr flight + direct bus ($70-$130).
details.Safety: Generally safe campus, though standard college-town property crime and party-area dynamics exist.

test_scores.policy: Not required for admission, but considered if submitted

profile.topology: Flat, grid-based desert campus with iconic palm-lined pedestrian walkways (The Mall) that make walking and biking extremely easy across the entire layout. Outdoors: Surrounded by dramatic mountain ranges (Catalinas and Rincons) offering incredible desert hiking, rock climbing, and mountain biking within 20-30 minutes; landlocked with no major lakes or ocean; winter skiing available at Mount Lemmon (1 hour away).
profile.airport_distance: 9 miles (~20 min drive) to Tucson International Airport (TUS).
profile.transit_options: Sun Tran bus system and the modern Sun Link Streetcar running directly through campus and downtown Tucson.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: Urban-suburban desert setting. The campus blends directly into the vibrant Main Gate Square commercial district and is right next to the historic Fourth Avenue strip, offering local indie venues, casual taco shops, and a dense student-heavy off-campus grid.
profile.housing_status: Freshmen live in large-scale resort-style residence halls with heavy social integration. Off-campus housing is dominated by towering, high-rise luxury student apartment complexes clustered tightly around the edges of campus along Park Avenue and Speedway Boulevard, most within a 5-to-10 minute walk or scooter ride to class.
profile.medical_access: Full clinical access through Banner University Medical Center located adjacent to campus.

academics.carnegie_classification: R1 Doctoral University (Very High Research Activity - AAU Member)
academics.biology_and_pre_med: BIO5 Institute heavy-hitter; exceptional interdisciplinary labs, over $1B in research spending, and growing AZ bioscience ties.
academics.clinical_and_medical_access: Full clinical access through Banner University Medical Center located adjacent to campus.
academics.flagship_programs: Physiology, Medical Biology, Astronomy, Optical Sciences, Pharmacy.

details.Support: Solid standard public performance showing an 83% retention rate and a 66% graduation rate, supported by standard large-university frameworks.
details.Social: Massive Greek life, pool parties, and a wild bar scene on Fourth Ave.
details.Weather: ~175 nice days. Lovely winters but brutal Jun-Sep heat (110F+) penalized
details.Biology: BIO5 Institute heavy-hitter; exceptional interdisciplinary labs, pre-health tracks, and growing AZ bioscience ties.
details.CLS: Strong Physiology/Med Bio tracks; covers core chem/micro, but no direct main-campus MLS BS.
details.Spirit: Rivalry-fueled Wildcat sports culture; massive basketball tradition and rowdy football tailgates.

details.CultureShock: Desert sun, palm trees, and massive California student population; seamless cultural transition.
details.Outdoors: Great desert hiking and stargazing, but heavily landlocked and extremely hot.
details.Safety: Tucson urban proximity and regional border-city property stats pull down off-campus safety indexes.

profile.topology: Flat urban-suburban campus layout featuring broad pedestrian malls, open green spaces, and integrated light rail access across the Tempe metro. Outdoors: Right next to Tempe Town Lake for kayaking and paddleboarding; local hiking at 'A' Mountain (Papago Park) on campus borders; major mountain trails (Camelback/Superstitions) within 20-30 minutes; no nearby ocean or skiing (3+ hours to Flagstaff).
profile.airport_distance: 7 miles (~10-15 min drive) to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX).
profile.transit_options: Valley Metro Light Rail station directly on campus alongside extensive local bus routes and free neighborhood circulators.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A bustling urban city environment centered right next to downtown Tempe. Mill Avenue runs parallel to campus with high-rise bars, shopping, and restaurants, creating an energetic city vibe that seamlessly merges with the massive student population.
profile.housing_status: Modern residential 'villages' cluster freshmen tightly by major. Off-campus housing consists of sprawling high-rise apartment towers lining University Drive and Apache Boulevard, many featuring resort-style pools and private shuttle options to combat the desert heat.
profile.medical_access: Integrated health services on-campus and close proximity to Valley-wide clinical networks.

academics.biology_and_pre_med: Biodesign Institute engine; cutting-edge research facilities and direct health-tech pipelines in the Phoenix metro.
academics.clinical_and_medical_access: Integrated health services on-campus and close proximity to Valley-wide clinical networks.
academics.flagship_programs: Medical Laboratory Science (BAS with NAACLS accreditation), Biomedical Engineering, Sustainability, Nursing.

details.CultureShock: Sunny year-round, giant SoCal transplant crowd, and familiar desert/coastal lifestyle blend.
details.Outdoors: Highly urbanized; great city amenities but requires driving out of the metro for real nature escapes.
details.GoHome: Easy: 5.5hr drive (~$55 gas) or 3.5hr trip via 1.25hr flight ($40-$80).

profile.topology: Flat, historic, and beautifully shaded campus centered around 'The Oval,' with dedicated bike lanes and extremely easy pedestrian navigation. Outdoors: Immediate access to Horsetooth Reservoir for boating/paddleboarding; world-class mountain biking and hiking trails directly bordering the foothills; skiing in the Rockies (Estes Park/Loveland) within 1 to 1.5 hours.
profile.airport_distance: 65 miles (~1 hr 15 min drive) north to Denver International Airport (DEN), with convenient Bustang shuttle options.
profile.transit_options: MAX Bus Rapid Transit system running directly through campus, connecting Fort Collins from north to south.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A classic, thriving Colorado mountain town. The campus sits a short, scenic bike ride away from historic 'Old Town' Fort Collins, which features Victorian-style brick storefronts, local craft breweries, and an extremely friendly, outdoors-oriented community feel.
profile.housing_status: Freshman housing features robust residential learning communities on campus. Off-campus options consist largely of multi-family rental houses and mid-rise complexes stretching toward Old Town, where biking or taking the MAX bus makes commuting seamless.
profile.medical_access: Clinical partnerships with UCHealth Medical Center of the Rockies and local regional clinics.

academics.clinical_and_medical_access: Clinical partnerships with UCHealth Medical Center of the Rockies and local regional clinics.
academics.flagship_programs: Microbiology (CCMLS Clinical Feeder Track), Veterinary Medicine, Biomedical Sciences, Environmental Health.

details.Social: Laid-back brewery and live music town; missing the massive blowout party reputation.

details.CLS: Microbiology BS has strong clinical tracks and a direct feeder partnership with CCMLS.
details.Spirit: Loud Ram pride with a modern on-campus stadium, but regional and lacks the massive, all-consuming SEC game-day culture.

details.CultureShock: Great laid-back outdoor culture; feels slightly more local/traditional Colorado than Boulder.

details.Safety: Fort Collins consistently ranks among the safest mid-sized cities and campuses in the country.

profile.topology: Compact, historic urban-campus layout featuring brick pathways, shaded quads (The Horseshoe), and relatively flat walking terrain. Outdoors: Access to the Congaree River and Lake Murray for kayaking and boating; flat local wooded trails, but no significant mountains or skiing within a reasonable day trip; coastal beaches are roughly 2 hours away.
profile.airport_distance: 7 miles (~15 min drive) to Columbia Metropolitan Airport (CAE).
profile.transit_options: COMET bus system and student-operated shuttles offering reliable connectivity across campus and downtown Columbia.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A classic Southern state-capital city setting. The campus weaves directly into downtown Columbia and is right next to the historic 'Five Points' district—a lively neighborhood strip filled with local bars, eateries, and Southern storefronts.
profile.housing_status: Freshman housing features historic halls around The Horseshoe as well as massive modern residential complexes like Green Quad. Off-campus housing is heavily influenced by Greek village houses and managed student apartments spread across downtown and the Vista district.
profile.medical_access: Integrated student health and access to Prisma Health hospital systems.

academics.clinical_and_medical_access: Integrated student health and direct access to Prisma Health Richland hospital systems.
academics.flagship_programs: International Business (#1 Nationally), Biological Sciences, Pre-Med / Nursing, Marine Science.

profile.topology: Flat, historic Pacific Northwest campus featuring towering old-growth trees, brick architecture, and extensive dedicated bike paths. Outdoors: Instant access to the Willamette River and McDonald-Dunn Forest for trail running and mountain biking; Cascade Mountains and skiing (Hoodoo/Willamette Pass) within 1 to 1.5 hours; Pacific Ocean beaches are roughly 1 hour west.
profile.airport_distance: 45 miles (~50 min drive) north to Eugene Airport (EUG) or 90 miles to Portland International (PDX).
profile.transit_options: Corvallis Transit System (CTS) provides fareless local bus service across the entire city and campus footprint.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A quintessential, peaceful Pacific Northwest college town. Downtown Corvallis sits right next to the Willamette River with indie coffee shops and local bookstores, creating an unhurried, bike-centric, and intensely green community feel.
profile.housing_status: Freshman housing features diverse residence halls across campus. Off-campus housing consists primarily of affordable local apartment complexes and cozy rental houses scattered through quiet neighborhoods where biking is the default transit method.
profile.medical_access: Access via Good Samaritan Regional Medical Center and university-affiliated health clinics.

academics.flagship_programs: BioHealth Sciences (Pre-Clinical Lab Science Track), Biochemistry, Forestry, Oceanography.

profile.topology: Built on a mesa with distinct slopes and stairways connecting upper and lower campus, but compact enough to cross on foot in 20 minutes. profile.topology: Hillside campus nestled against the Wasatch Range, featuring sloping terrain, scenic elevated views of Salt Lake City, and modern architectural clusters. details.Spirit: Peak SEC tradition; Toomers Corner, legendary tailgating, and total town-wide football immersion.
details.Admissions: Hard (D Grade): Competitive out-of-state pool (~50% acceptance rate); admissions leans heavily on GPA metrics and academic alignment.
details.CultureShock: Significant shift to SEC Greek life, traditional Southern pacing, and a completely different social ecosystem.
details.Outdoors: Local state parks, rolling hills, and lake access within 20-30 minutes.
details.GoHome: Hard: 7.5hr trip via flight + shuttle; expensive ($200-$400+).
details.Safety: Quiet, traditional, highly secure southern college town environment.

profile.topology: Flat, highly walkable, and tree-lined campus with historic brick quadrangles and modern sustainability-focused facilities. Outdoors: Bordered by the Willamette River and Skinner Butte for quick trail runs; Cascade Mountains and winter skiing (Hoodoo/Willamette Pass) within 1 to 1.5 hours; Pacific Coast beaches are roughly 1 hour west.
profile.airport_distance: 10 miles (~15 min drive) to Eugene Airport (EUG).
profile.transit_options: Lane Transit District (LTD) bus network offering free rides for UO students across the Eugene-Springfield area.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A progressive Pacific Northwest city-town hybrid. The campus borders the lively West University neighborhood, which is packed with local food trucks, coffee houses, and indie vintage stores, carrying a distinctively artsy, green, and bike-heavy culture.
profile.housing_status: Freshmen live in modern residence halls close to the Erb Memorial Union. Off-campus housing consists heavily of shared student rentals and mid-rise apartment buildings throughout the West University district within easy walking or biking distance.
profile.medical_access: Integrated student health and proximity to Eugene-area medical and trauma centers.

academics.carnegie_classification: R1 Doctoral University (Very High Research Activity - AAU Member)
academics.biology_and_pre_med: Respectable molecular biology and neuroscience via the Institute of Molecular Biology; active undergraduate lab involvement.
academics.clinical_and_medical_access: Integrated student health and proximity to Eugene-area medical and trauma centers.
academics.flagship_programs: Human Physiology, Molecular Biology, Neuroscience, Sports Business.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$68,931 - $74,325 (Out-of-State). Does not participate in WUE, but offers automatic Apex/Summit merit scholarships based on GPA. Cost could lower.
details.Support: Dependable regional public framework featuring an 85% retention rate and a 70% graduation rate.
details.Social: Strong house party and bar scene, but lacks the sheer massive scale of ASU or LSU.
details.Weather: ~105 nice days. Wet PNW marine climate, relentlessly grey
details.Biology: Respectable molecular biology and neuroscience (Institute of Molecular Biology), but smaller overall scope than peers.
details.CLS: Solid West Coast bio/micro curriculum; covers general prereqs, though lacks on-campus MLS.
details.Spirit: Iconic Autzen Stadium noise, Nike-backed hype, and massive statewide Duck pride.
details.Admissions: Target: ~78% acceptance rate; holistic review that places solid value on AP course load and personal statement essays. GPAs between 3.4-3.7
details.CultureShock: West Coast outdoorsy vibe; heavily aligned with SoCal lifestyle values despite the regional shift.
details.Outdoors: Deep PNW recreation in the Cascades, though winter rain dampens daily outdoor activities.
details.Safety: Eugene has typical Pacific Northwest property crime issues, but campus operations are tightly managed.

test_scores.policy: Not required for admission, but considered if submitted

profile.topology: Expansive, flat Southern campus featuring magnificent live oak trees, Italian Renaissance-style architecture, and picturesque lakes. Outdoors: Situated right along the Mississippi River with campus lakes for walking; virtually zero dynamic elevation, mountains, or skiing; Gulf Coast beaches are 2+ hours south.
profile.airport_distance: 9 miles (~15 min drive) to Baton Rouge Metropolitan Airport (BTR) or 75 miles to New Orleans (MSY).
profile.transit_options: Tiger Trails campus bus service connecting students across all residential and academic zones.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A sprawling Southern capital city setting. The campus is self-contained along the Mississippi River, bordered by suburban residential extensions and bustling commercial corridors characterized by heavy local Southern culture and legendary game-day energy.
profile.housing_status: Freshman housing features historic and modern residential colleges across campus. Off-campus housing is dominated by sprawling luxury apartment complexes and rental properties off Highland Road and Burbank Drive, which require driving or shuttle utilization to reach central classes.
profile.medical_access: Access to comprehensive university medical clinics and proximity to Baton Rouge General health systems.

academics.carnegie_classification: R1 Doctoral University (Very High Research Activity)
academics.biology_and_pre_med: Established Biological Sciences department with direct pipelines into LSU Health Sciences Centers in New Orleans and Shreveport.
academics.clinical_and_medical_access: Access to comprehensive university medical clinics and proximity to Baton Rouge General health systems.
academics.flagship_programs: Medical Laboratory Science (MLS Pipeline via LSU Health), Biological Sciences, Coastal Geology, Veterinary Medicine.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$56,122 - $58,256 (Out-of-State). Offers automatic non-resident merit scholarships and fee waivers for high GPAs and test scores. Cost could lower.
details.Support: Standard SEC foundational support systems with an 85% retention rate and a 69% graduation rate.
details.Social: Tigerland and SEC tailgating create one of the most intense party environments in the country.
details.Weather: ~95 nice days. Subtropical humidity makes bad days genuinely oppressive
details.Biology: Solid regional bio departments and local medical ties, but institutional biotech research funding is relatively limited.
details.CLS: Has an established Medical Laboratory Science pipeline linked directly to LSU Health Sciences.
details.Spirit: Unrivaled Death Valley night games, legendary Cajun tailgating, and pure football-as-religion culture.
details.Admissions: Target: Straightforward benchmarks with ~79% acceptance rate, Typical admitted students have weighted GPAs between 3.4–3.7
details.CultureShock: Largest cultural shift on the list: heavy Cajun/subtropical environment, unique local customs, and deep-rooted SEC identity.
details.Outdoors: Flat, swampy, and intensely humid; virtually zero traditional dynamic outdoor recreation.
details.GoHome: Hard: 9hr trip via multi-leg flights; very expensive ($325-$525+).
details.Safety: Baton Rouge consistently registers high violent and property crime rates per capita, requiring extreme off-campus vigilance.

profile.topology: Flat, tropical South Florida campus layout featuring modern architecture, sunny outdoor courtyards, and close proximity to coastal waterways. Outdoors: Minutes from Atlantic Ocean beaches for swimming, surfing, and paddleboarding; flat local coastal paths, but zero mountains or skiing anywhere in Florida (completely flat terrain).
profile.airport_distance: 26 miles (~30 min drive) to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (FLL) or Palm Beach International (PBI).
profile.transit_options: Boca Raton Tri-Rail shuttle service connecting students directly to regional transit systems and local commercial centers.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: An upscale, quiet suburban South Florida setting. The campus sits in wealthy Boca Raton just minutes from pristine Atlantic beaches and high-end outdoor malls, carrying a relaxed, palm-lined coastal vibe rather than a dense, walkable college town feel.
profile.housing_status: Freshmen live in modern resort-style residence halls like Innovation Village Apartments. Off-campus housing is expensive and upscale, dominated by suburban rental units and luxury apartment complexes across Boca Raton where most students require a car to get around.
profile.medical_access: Access to local university health services and proximal to regional Baptist Health networks.

academics.carnegie_classification: R1 Doctoral University (Very High Research Activity)
academics.biology_and_pre_med: Solid regional Florida pre-health tracks, Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine on campus, and strong marine science research.
academics.clinical_and_medical_access: Access to local university health services and proximal to regional Baptist Health networks.
academics.flagship_programs: Biological Sciences, Pre-Med / Neuroscience, Marine Biology, Nursing.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$42,382 - $46,422 (Out-of-State). Offers non-resident merit scholarships based on GPA. Cost could lower after admission.
details.Support: Developing completion infrastructure reflecting an 80% retention rate and a ~50-53% graduation rate, tracking slightly behind major flagships.
details.Social: Sleepy campus in a wealthy suburb; requires a drive to Miami/Fort Lauderdale for real nightlife.
details.Weather: ~175 nice days. Beautiful winters but summer humidity and hurricane risk penalized
details.Biology: Decent regional Florida pre-health tracks, but lacks a heavy research corridor or major biotech pipeline.
details.CLS: Solid Medical Biology tracks; good access to regional Florida hospital MLS internship sites.
details.Spirit: Subdued athletic culture; smaller commuter crowds and minimal traditional game-day energy.
details.Admissions: Target: ~60% acceptance rate and typical admitted students have weighted GPAs between 3.2–3.5
details.CultureShock: Familiar sunny coastal/beach lifestyle, but a distinct East Coast/suburban adjustment away from the West Coast vibe.
details.Outdoors: Top-tier coastal and water lifestyle with Atlantic beaches and intracoastal waterways 10-15 minutes away.
details.Safety: Boca Raton is generally safe, but open regional commuter access introduces consistent property crime profiles.

test_scores.policy: Required to be considered for admission

profile.topology: Sprawling, flat urban-suburban South Florida campus layout featuring modern architecture and lush tropical landscaping. Outdoors: Minutes from the Everglades and a short drive to Miami beaches for swimming and coastal recreation; flat local landscape with zero mountains or skiing anywhere in Florida.
profile.airport_distance: 12 miles (~20-25 min drive) to Miami International Airport (MIA).
profile.transit_options: FIUs Panther Express shuttle system and local Miami-Dade transit buses connecting students across the metro region.
profile.neighborhood_vibe: A massive urban-suburban setting in West Miami. The campus acts as a dense, high-energy city hub surrounded by vibrant South Florida culture, dense commercial corridors, and immediate access to Miami.
profile.housing_status: Freshman housing features large modern residential complexes like Parkview and University Towers. Off-campus housing consists heavily of dense student apartment complexes and suburban rentals across the Miami metro, requiring cars or shuttles for transit.
profile.medical_access: Full clinical integration anchored directly by the Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine and extensive partnerships with Baptist Health and Jackson Health System.

academics.carnegie_classification: R1 Doctoral University (Very High Research Activity)
academics.biology_and_pre_med: R1 research infrastructure with solid federal funding and clinical medical school networks on campus.
academics.clinical_and_medical_access: Full clinical integration anchored directly by the Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine and extensive partnerships with Baptist Health and Jackson Health System.
academics.flagship_programs: Biological Sciences, Biomedical Engineering, Public Health, Nursing.

details.Cost: Est. Total COA: ~$41,500 - $45,000 (Out-of-State). Offers competitive non-resident merit scholarships based on GPA and test scores.
details.Support: Massive institutional scale operating with an 89% freshman retention rate, though large student-to-adviser ratios impact upper-division navigation.
details.Social: On-campus social life is severely limited by a massive commuter culture.
details.Weather: ~175 nice days. Sunny tropical winters, but heavy summer humidity and hurricane season risks.
details.Biology: R1 research infrastructure with solid federal funding and clinical medical school networks, though trailing elite West Coast biological powerhouses.
details.CLS: Solid biological tracks and Biomedical Engineering intersections, with clinical exposure via major Miami hospital networks.
details.Spirit: Growing Conference USA athletic presence, but largely a commuter-heavy vibe lacking traditional all-consuming sports culture.
details.Admissions: Target: ~60% acceptance rate; selective index-based review heavily weighting GPA and test scores, SAT required
details.CultureShock: High-energy urban Miami demographic shift; intense cultural melting pot distinctly different from Southern California pacing.
details.Outdoors: Great coastal and beach access in Miami, though completely flat with zero elevation or mountain recreation.
details.GoHome: Hard: 7.5hr trip via 5hr flight + transit; expensive tickets ($180-$320).
details.Safety: Suburban campus footprint with standard major metropolitan property and urban crime considerations in the surrounding Miami area.
